visualCharacteristics.description: Plain data table inside long legal text (contracts, promotion rules): header-like first row, thin row rules, rich-text cells.

contentPattern: One block row per table row, one cell per column (1-5 columns). Cells hold rich text (paragraphs, bold, line breaks, links). The first row renders as the header row (<th scope=col>) unless the no-header option is set. A row may have fewer cells than the widest row (source colspan): its last cell spans the remaining columns.
usage: Legal data tables in contracts and promotion regulations (e.g. /contratos/contrato-nucel-plano-35-gb: 10 tables up to 5 columns; /contratos/regulamento-da-promocao-usou-ganhou-no-cartao-nu-empresas: 4-column tables).
reuseGuidance: Use for any genuine tabular data (rows x columns of text). Source tables without <th> whose first row reads as a header map to the default (header) form; use no-header when the first row is data. Not for layout grids (use columns) or key/value notes (use notice).

importShape.headerRow: First block row = block name only: 'Table', or 'Table (striped)' / 'Table (bordered, no-header)' for options.
importShape.rows: Every following block row = one source <tr>. Cell 0 is the row component id chosen by that row's own cell count N: N=1 'table-row', N=2..5 'table-col-N'. Cells 1..N are the source <td>/<th> contents in order (colspan dropped; the block JS restores the span).
importShape.cells:
Each content cell starts with a field hint comment '' (K = 1-based column index) followed by the cell's rich text (keep

, , ,
, ; unwrap

/). Empty source cells still get their cell with only the field hint so column positions stay aligned.
rules: Never omit the row component id cell: md2jcr treats a single-cell first body row as block (parent) properties, and the id is what selects the N-column row model.
Do not emit more than 5 content cells per row; the model supports up to 5 columns.
Do not wrap the first row in <th>; the block decides header rendering from the no-header option.
